categories.main_business_segments: ELV (formerly Anthem, Inc.) operates through four main business segments: Commercial & Specialty Business (offering health plans and specialty insurance to individuals and employer groups), Government Business (serving Medicare, Medicaid, and Federal Employee Health Benefits members), IngenioRx (pharmacy benefit management services), and Other (including the Diversified Business Group focused on health services and care delivery innovation).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced digital platforms, data analytics, and integrated care management programs to deliver health benefits and services. It employs managed care models, value-based provider contracting, medical management programs, and proprietary actuarial and pricing methodologies. IngenioRx utilizes formulary management, pharmacy networks, and mail order capabilities, while the Diversified Business Group develops new care delivery and payment models.
categories.primary_customers_markets: ELV serves a broad range of customers including individuals, employer groups (both risk-based and fee-based), federal and state government agencies (Medicare, Medicaid, FEHB), and unaffiliated health plans. Key end markets include commercial health insurance, government-sponsored health programs, and pharmacy benefit management for both affiliated and external clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates across the United States, serving as the Blue Cross or Blue Cross and Blue Shield licensee in 14 states and Puerto Rico, and providing services in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico through its subsidiaries. It has a particularly strong presence in states like California, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, New York, Ohio, Texas, and Virginia.
categories.supply_chain_position: ELV primarily operates downstream in the healthcare supply chain as a health benefits provider and pharmacy benefit manager, interfacing directly with end customers (employers, individuals, government programs) and managing relationships with healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding government-sponsored business, integrating medical and pharmacy benefits, driving value-based care, digital transformation, and optimizing operational efficiency. The company invests in digital engagement platforms, care management tools, and data analytics, and pursues acquisitions to enhance capabilities in home-based care, behavioral health, and specialty services.
categories.revenue_model: ELV generates revenue primarily through insurance premiums from risk-based health plans, administrative fees from fee-based (ASO) customers, product revenue from pharmacy benefit management, and specialty insurance products. Additional revenue streams include government contracts, care management services, and ancillary health products.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include UnitedHealth Group, CVS Health/Aetna, Cigna, Humana, and Centene. ELV is one of the largest health benefits companies in the U.S. by medical membership and is typically the market leader in its Blue Cross and Blue Shield service areas, leveraging strong brand recognition and extensive provider networks.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2021, ELV reported $136.9 billion in operating revenue and $6.1 billion in net income, serving over 45 million medical members. The company demonstrated strong growth, with operating revenue increasing 13.4% year-over-year, driven by government business expansion and acquisitions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: ELV emphasizes a whole-health approach, integrating medical, pharmacy, behavioral, and specialty benefits to improve outcomes and affordability. Its value proposition centers on local market expertise combined with national scale, broad provider networks, innovative digital tools, and a commitment to value-based care and quality improvement.
